There's part of an invading force already landed: we must lean toward the King. I will look for him and secretly relieve him. You go and keep up the conversation with the Duke, so that my act of charity may not be perceived by him. If he asks for me, I am ill, and gone to bed. If I die for it, as no less is threatened me, the King my old master must be relieved. There is some strange business afoot, Edmund; please be careful.
[Exit.]

EDMUND. This courtesy, forbidden to you, the Duke shall instantly know about — and about that letter too. This seems a fair deserving, and must bring me what my father loses, no less than all: the younger rises when the old falls.
[Exit.]

chapters.title: Act 3, Scene 4 — A part of the Heath with a Hovel
paragraphs: [Storm continues. Enter LEAR, KENT, and FOOL.]
KENT. Here is the place, my lord; good my lord, go in. The tyranny of the open night is too rough for human nature to endure.
LEAR. Leave me alone.
KENT. Good my lord, enter here.
LEAR. Will you break my heart?
KENT. I had rather break my own. Good my lord, enter.

LEAR. You think it's a great matter that this contentious storm invades us to the skin. So it is, to you; but where the greater malady is fixed, the lesser is scarcely felt. You would shun a bear, but if your flight lay toward the raging sea, you would meet the bear face to face. When the mind is free, the body is delicate. The tempest in my mind takes from my senses all feeling besides what beats there: filial ingratitude! Is it not as if this mouth should tear this hand for lifting food to it? But I will punish them to the heart. No, I will weep no more. On such a night to shut me out! Pour on; I will endure. On such a night as this! Oh Regan, Goneril! Your old kind father, whose frank heart gave all — oh, that way madness lies; let me shun that; no more of that.
KENT. Good my lord, enter here.
LEAR. Please go in yourself; seek your own comfort. This tempest won't give me leave to ponder on things that would hurt me more. But I'll go in.
[To the FOOL.] In, boy; go first. You houseless poverty —
Go on, get inside. I'll pray, and then I'll sleep.
[FOOL goes in.]

Poor naked wretches, wherever you are, who endure the pelting of this pitiless storm, how shall your houseless heads and unfed sides, your ragged clothes full of holes and gaps, defend you from seasons like these? Oh, I have taken too little care of this! Take your medicine, pomp; expose yourself to feel what wretches feel, so that you may shake the superfluity to them, and show the heavens more just.
EDGAR.
[Within.] Fathom and a half, fathom and a half! Poor Tom!
[The FOOL runs out of the hovel.]
FOOL. Don't come in here, nuncle, here's a spirit. Help me, help me!
KENT. Give me your hand. Who's there?
FOOL. A spirit, a spirit: he says his name is poor Tom.
KENT. What are you that grumble there in the straw? Come out.
[Enter EDGAR, disguised as a madman.]
EDGAR. Away! The foul fiend follows me! Through the sharp hawthorn blows the cold wind. Humh! Go to your cold bed, and warm yourself.
LEAR. Did you give all to your two daughters? And have you come to this?

EDGAR. Who gives anything to poor Tom? Whom the foul fiend has led through fire and through flame, through ford and whirlpool, over bog and quagmire; who has laid knives under his pillow and halters in his pew, set rat-poison by his porridge; made him proud of heart, to ride on a bay trotting horse over four-inch bridges, to chase his own shadow as if it were a traitor. Bless your five wits! Tom's a-cold. Oh, do, de, do, de, do, de. Bless you from whirlwinds, star-blasting, and being snatched! Do poor Tom some charity, whom the foul fiend torments. There I could have him now, and there — and there again, and there.
[Storm continues.]
LEAR. What, have his daughters brought him to this state? Could you save nothing? Did you give them all?
FOOL. No, he kept a blanket, or we'd all have been ashamed.
LEAR. Now may all the plagues that in the hanging air await men's faults fall upon your daughters!
KENT. He has no daughters, sir.

LEAR. Death, traitor! Nothing could have subdued nature to such a lowness but his unkind daughters. Is it the fashion that discarded fathers should have so little mercy on their flesh? Judicious punishment! It was this flesh that begot those pelican daughters.
EDGAR. Pillicock sat on Pillicock hill, alow, alow, loo loo!
FOOL. This cold night will turn us all to fools and madmen.
EDGAR. Beware of the foul fiend: obey your parents; keep your word truly; swear not; commit not adultery with a man's sworn spouse; set not your sweetheart on proud finery. Tom's a-cold.
LEAR. What were you?

EDGAR. A serving-man, proud in heart and mind; who curled my hair; wore gloves in my cap; served the lust of my mistress' heart, and did the act of darkness with her; swore as many oaths as I spoke words, and broke them in the sweet face of heaven. One who slept while plotting lust, and waked to do it. Wine I loved deeply, dice dearly; and in matters of women out-pampered the Turk. False of heart, light of ear, bloody of hand; a hog in sloth, a fox in stealth, a wolf in greediness, a dog in madness, a lion in prey. Don't let the creaking of shoes nor the rustling of silks betray your poor heart to woman. Keep your foot out of brothels, your hand out of women's plackets, your pen from a moneylender's book, and defy the foul fiend. Still through the hawthorn blows the cold wind: says suum, mun, nonny. Dauphin my boy, boy, sessa! Let him trot by.
[Storm still continues.]

LEAR. Why, you'd be better off in your grave than to face with your uncovered body this extremity of the skies. Is man no more than this? Consider him well. You owe the worm no silk, the beast no hide, the sheep no wool, the cat no perfume. Ha! Here are three of us who are sophisticated! You are the thing itself: unaccommodated man is no more than such a poor, bare, forked animal as you are. Off, off, you borrowings! Come, unbutton here.
[Tears off his clothes.]

FOOL. Please, nuncle, be content. It's a wicked night to swim in. Now a little fire in a wild field would be like an old lecher's heart, a small spark with all the rest of his body cold. Look, here comes a walking fire.

EDGAR. This is the foul fiend Flibbertigibbet. He begins at curfew, and walks till the first cockcrow. He gives the cataract and the cyst, squints the eye, and makes the harelip; he mildews the white wheat, and hurts the poor creature of earth. Saint Withold walked the moor thrice; he met the nightmare and her nine offspring; bade her dismount and pledge her word, and out with you, witch, out with you!
KENT. How fares your grace?
[Enter GLOUCESTER with a torch.]
LEAR. Who's that?
KENT. Who's there? What is it you seek?
GLOUCESTER. What are you there? Your names?

EDGAR. Poor Tom; who eats the swimming frog, the toad, the tadpole, the wall-newt and the water-newt; who in the fury of his heart, when the foul fiend rages, eats cow-dung for salads; swallows the old rat and the dead dog in the ditch; drinks the green scum on a stagnant pool; who is whipped from parish to parish, and stocked, punished, and imprisoned; who has had three suits to his back, six shirts to his body, a horse to ride, and a weapon to wear. But mice and rats and such small game have been Tom's food for seven long years. Beware my follower. Peace, Smulkin; peace, you fiend!
GLOUCESTER. What, has your grace no better company?
EDGAR. The prince of darkness is a gentleman: Modo he's called, and Mahu.
GLOUCESTER. Our flesh and blood, my lord, has grown so vile that it hates what begets it.
EDGAR. Poor Tom's a-cold.

GLOUCESTER. Go in with me. My duty cannot suffer me to obey in all your daughters' hard commands; though their injunction is to bar my doors, and let this tyrannous night take hold of you, yet I have ventured to come seek you out, and bring you where both fire and food are ready.
LEAR. First let me talk with this philosopher. What is the cause of thunder?
KENT. Good my lord, take his offer; go into the house.
LEAR. I'll talk a word with this same learned Theban. What is your study?
EDGAR. How to prevent the fiend and to kill vermin.
LEAR. Let me ask you one word in private.
KENT. Importune him once more to go, my lord; his wits begin to unsettle.

GLOUCESTER. Can you blame him? His daughters seek his death. Ah, that good Kent! He said it would be thus, poor banished man! You say the King grows mad; I'll tell you, friend, I am almost mad myself. I had a son, now outlawed from my blood; he sought my life only lately, very lately. I loved him, friend, no father loved his son more dearly. To tell you the truth,
[Storm continues.]
the grief has crazed my wits. What a night this is! I do beseech your grace —
LEAR. Oh, I beg your pardon, sir. Noble philosopher, your company.
EDGAR. Tom's a-cold.
GLOUCESTER. In, fellow, there, into the hovel; keep yourself warm.
LEAR. Come, let's all in.
KENT. This way, my lord.
LEAR. With him; I will keep still with my philosopher.
KENT. Good my lord, indulge him; let him take the fellow.
GLOUCESTER. You take him along.
KENT. Sirrah, come on; go along with us.
LEAR. Come, good Athenian.
GLOUCESTER. No words, no words, hush.
EDGAR. Child Rowland to the dark tower came, his word was still — Fie, foh, and fum, I smell the blood of a British man.
[Exeunt.]

chapters.title: Act 3, Scene 5 — A Room in Gloucester’s Castle
paragraphs: [Enter CORNWALL and EDMUND.]
CORNWALL. I will have my revenge before I leave his house.
EDMUND. How, my lord, I may be censured, that nature thus gives way to loyalty, something makes me afraid to think of.
CORNWALL. I now perceive it was not altogether your brother's evil disposition that made him seek his death; but a provoking merit, set to work by a reprehensible badness in himself.

EDMUND. How malicious is my fortune, that I must repent of being just! This is the letter he spoke of, which proves him an informing party to the advantages of France. Oh heavens! That this treason did not exist; or that I were not the one to detect it!
CORNWALL. Come with me to the Duchess.
EDMUND. If the matter of this paper be certain, you have mighty business in hand.
CORNWALL. True or false, it has made you Earl of Gloucester. Seek out where your father is, that he may be ready for our arrest.
EDMUND.
[Aside.] If I find him comforting the King, it will stuff his
suspicion more fully. I will persevere in my course of loyalty, though the conflict be sharp between that and my blood.
CORNWALL. I will place trust in you; and you shall find a dearer father in my love.
[Exeunt.]

chapters.title: Act 3, Scene 6 — A Chamber in a Farmhouse adjoining the Castle
paragraphs: [Enter GLOUCESTER, LEAR, KENT, FOOL, and EDGAR.]
GLOUCESTER. Here is better than the open air; accept it gratefully. I will piece out the comfort with whatever I can add. I will not be long away from you.
KENT. All the power of his wits has given way to his impatience. The gods reward your kindness!
[Exit GLOUCESTER.]
EDGAR. Frateretto calls me; and tells me Nero is an angler in the lake of darkness. Pray, innocent, and beware the foul fiend.
FOOL. Please, nuncle, tell me whether a madman is a gentleman or a yeoman.
LEAR. A king, a king!
FOOL. No, he's a yeoman who has a gentleman for his son; for he's a mad yeoman who sees his son become a gentleman before he does.
LEAR. To have a thousand devils with red-hot burning spits come hissing in upon them.
EDGAR. The foul fiend bites my back.
FOOL. He's mad who trusts in the tameness of a wolf, the health of a horse, the love of a boy, or the oath of a whore.
LEAR. It shall be done. I will put them on trial straight away.
[To EDGAR.] Come, sit you here, most learned justice;
[To the FOOL.] You, wise sir, sit here. Now, you she-foxes! —
EDGAR. Look where he stands and glares! Do you want eyes at your trial, madam? Come over the stream, Bessy, to me.
FOOL. Her boat has a leak, and she must not speak why she dares not come over to you.
EDGAR. The foul fiend haunts poor Tom in the voice of a nightingale. Hoppedance cries in Tom's belly for two white herrings. Croak not, black angel; I have no food for you.
KENT. How are you, sir? Don't stand so dazed. Will you lie down and rest upon the cushions?
LEAR. I'll see their trial first. Bring in their evidence.
[To EDGAR.] You, robed man of justice, take your place.
[To the FOOL.] And you, his yoke-fellow of equity,
sit on the bench beside him. [To KENT.] You are of the commission; sit you too.
EDGAR. Let us deal justly. Sleepest or wakest you, jolly shepherd? Your sheep are in the corn; and for one blast of your tiny mouth your sheep shall take no harm. Purr! The cat is grey.
LEAR. Arraign her first; it's Goneril. I here take my oath before this honourable assembly, she kicked the poor King her father.
FOOL. Come here, mistress. Is your name Goneril?
LEAR. She cannot deny it.
FOOL. I beg your pardon, I took you for a joint-stool.
LEAR. And here's another, whose warped looks proclaim what stock her heart is made of. Stop her there! Arms, arms! Sword! Fire! Corruption in the court! False justice, why have you let her escape?
EDGAR. Bless your five wits!
KENT. Oh pity! Sir, where is the patience now that you so often boasted of keeping?
EDGAR.
[Aside.] My tears begin to take his part so much
they spoil my disguise.
LEAR. The little dogs and all — Trey, Blanch, and Sweetheart — see, they bark at me.

EDGAR. Tom will throw his head at them. Away, you curs! Be your mouth either black or white, tooth that poisons if it bite; mastiff, greyhound, mongrel grim, hound or spaniel, bitch or him, or bobtail mutt or trundle-tail — Tom will make them weep and wail; for, with throwing my head thus, dogs leap the hatch, and all are fled. Do, de, de, de. Sessa! Come, march to wakes and fairs and market towns. Poor Tom, your drinking-horn is dry.

LEAR. Then let them dissect Regan; see what breeds about her heart. Is there any cause in nature that makes these hard hearts? [To EDGAR.] You, sir, I retain as one of my hundred; only I do not like the fashion of your garments. You'll say they are Persian; but let them be changed.
KENT. Now, good my lord, lie here and rest a while.
LEAR. Make no noise, make no noise; draw the curtains. So, so. We'll go to supper in the morning.
FOOL. And I'll go to bed at noon.
[Enter GLOUCESTER.]
GLOUCESTER. Come here, friend. Where is the King, my master?
KENT. Here, sir; but don't trouble him, his wits are gone.

GLOUCESTER. Good friend, I beg you, take him in your arms. I have overheard a plot of death against him. There is a litter ready; lay him in it, and drive towards Dover, friend, where you'll meet both welcome and protection. Take up your master. If you should delay half an hour, his life, with yours, and all who try to defend him, stand in certain loss. Take him up, take him up; and follow me, who will give you swift conduct to some provisions.
KENT. Oppressed nature sleeps. This rest might yet have soothed your broken sinews, which, if circumstance will not allow, will be hard to cure. Come, help to bear your master;
[To the FOOL.] You must not stay behind.
GLOUCESTER. Come, come, away!
[Exeunt KENT, GLOUCESTER, and the FOOL bearing off LEAR.]

EDGAR. When we see our betters bearing our woes, we scarcely think our miseries our foes. He who alone suffers, suffers most in the mind, leaving free things and happy shows behind. But then the mind much suffering does overleap when grief has mates, and bearing fellowship. How light and bearable my pain seems now, when that which makes me bend makes the King bow; he made childless as I was made fatherless! Tom, away! Mark the high noises, and reveal yourself, when false opinion, whose wrong thoughts defile you, in your just vindication reverses and reconciles you. Whatever else may happen tonight, may the King escape safely! Lurk, lurk.
[Exit.]

chapters.title: Act 3, Scene 7 — A Room in Gloucester’s Castle
paragraphs: [Enter CORNWALL, REGAN, GONERIL, EDMUND, and Servants.]
CORNWALL. Ride quickly to my lord, your husband; show him this letter. The army of France is landed. Seek out the traitor Gloucester.
[Exeunt some of the Servants.]
REGAN. Hang him instantly.
GONERIL. Pluck out his eyes.

CORNWALL. Leave him to my displeasure. Edmund, keep our sister company. The revenges we are bound to take upon your traitorous father are not fit for you to see. Advise the Duke, where you are going, to make most hasty preparation. We are bound to do the same. Our messengers shall be swift and intelligent between us. Farewell, dear sister, farewell, my lord of Gloucester.
[Enter OSWALD.]
What now! Where's the King?

OSWALD. My lord of Gloucester has carried him away. Some five or six and thirty of his knights, hot in pursuit of him, met him at the gate; who, with some others of the lord's household, are gone with him toward Dover, where they boast of having well-armed friends.
CORNWALL. Get horses for your mistress.
GONERIL. Farewell, sweet lord, and sister.
CORNWALL. Edmund, farewell.
[Exeunt GONERIL, EDMUND, and OSWALD.]
Go seek the traitor Gloucester, bind him like a thief, bring him before us.
[Exeunt other Servants.]
Though we may not lawfully pass sentence upon his life without the form of justice, yet our power shall do a courtesy to our wrath, which men may blame, but not control. Who's there? The traitor?
[Enter GLOUCESTER and Servants.]
REGAN. Ungrateful fox! It's he.
CORNWALL. Bind fast his withered arms.
GLOUCESTER. What do your graces mean? My good friends, consider that you are my guests. Do me no foul play, friends.
CORNWALL. Bind him, I say.
[Servants bind him.]
REGAN. Hard, hard. Oh, filthy traitor!
GLOUCESTER. Unmerciful lady though you are, I am no traitor.
CORNWALL. To this chair bind him. Villain, you shall find —
[REGAN plucks his beard.]
GLOUCESTER. By the kind gods, it's most ignobly done to pluck me by the beard.
REGAN. So white, and such a traitor!

GLOUCESTER. Wicked lady, these hairs that you tear from my chin will come to life and accuse you. I am your host. With robbers' hands you should not ruffle my hospitable favours like this. What will you do?
CORNWALL. Come, sir, what letters had you lately from France?
REGAN. Answer plainly, for we know the truth.
CORNWALL. And what alliance have you with the traitors lately landed in the kingdom?
REGAN. Into whose hands have you sent the lunatic King? Speak.
GLOUCESTER. I have a letter that was set down by guesswork, which came from someone of a neutral heart, and not from one who is opposed.
CORNWALL. Cunning.
REGAN. And false.
CORNWALL. Where have you sent the King?
GLOUCESTER. To Dover.
REGAN. Why to Dover? Were you not charged on penalty —
CORNWALL. Why to Dover? Let him first answer that.
GLOUCESTER. I am tied to the stake, and I must endure the course.
REGAN. Why to Dover, sir?

GLOUCESTER. Because I would not see your cruel nails pluck out his poor old eyes; nor your fierce sister stick boarish fangs in his anointed flesh. The sea, in such a storm as his bare head endured in hell-black night, would have risen up and quenched the stellar fires; yet, poor old heart, he helped the heavens rain. If wolves had howled at your gate at that grim time, you would have said, 'Good porter, turn the key.' All other cruelties relented; but I shall see the winged vengeance overtake such children.
CORNWALL. See it you never shall. Fellows, hold the chair. Upon these eyes of yours I'll set my foot.
[GLOUCESTER is held down in his chair, while CORNWALL plucks out one of his eyes and sets his foot on it.]
GLOUCESTER. He who hopes to live till he is old, give me some help! Oh cruel! Oh you gods!
REGAN. One side will mock the other; the other too!
CORNWALL. If you see vengeance —
FIRST SERVANT. Hold your hand, my lord. I have served you ever since I was a child; but I have never done you better service than now, to bid you stop.
REGAN. What's this, you dog!
FIRST SERVANT. If you wore a beard upon your chin, I'd shake it in this quarrel. What do you mean by this?
CORNWALL. My villain?
[Draws, and rushes at him.]
FIRST SERVANT. Nay then, come on, and take the chance of anger.
[Draws. They fight. CORNWALL is wounded.]
REGAN.
[To another servant.] Give me your sword. A peasant stand up like this?
[Snatches a sword, comes behind, and stabs him.]
FIRST SERVANT. Oh, I am slain! My lord, you have one eye left to see some misfortune on him. Oh!
[Dies.]
CORNWALL. Lest it see more, prevent it. Out, vile jelly! Where is your lustre now?
[Tears out GLOUCESTER's other eye and throws it on the ground.]
GLOUCESTER. All dark and comfortless. Where's my son Edmund? Edmund, kindle all the sparks of nature to avenge this horrid act.
REGAN. Out, treacherous villain! You call on him who hates you. It was he who exposed your treasons to us — who is too good to pity you.
GLOUCESTER. Oh my follies! Then Edgar was wronged. Kind gods, forgive me that, and prosper him!
REGAN. Thrust him out at the gates, and let him smell his way to Dover. How is it, my lord? How do you look?
CORNWALL. I have received a hurt. Follow me, lady. Turn out that eyeless villain. Throw this slave upon the dunghill. Regan, I bleed fast. This hurt comes at a bad time. Give me your arm.
[Exit CORNWALL, led by REGAN; Servants unbind GLOUCESTER and lead him out.]
SECOND SERVANT. I'll never care what wickedness I do, if this man comes to a good end.
THIRD SERVANT. If she lives long, and in the end meets the old course of death, women will all turn into monsters.
SECOND SERVANT. Let's follow the old Earl, and get the Bedlam beggar to lead him wherever he wants to go. His roguish madness lets him do anything.
THIRD SERVANT. You go; I'll fetch some flax and the whites of eggs to apply to his bleeding face. Now heaven help him!
[Exeunt.]

chapters.title: Act 4, Scene 1 — The heath
paragraphs: [Enter EDGAR.]

EDGAR. Yet better thus, and known to be despised, than still despised and flattered. To be the worst, the lowest and most dejected thing of fortune, stands still in hope, lives not in fear. The lamentable change is from the best; the worst returns to laughter. Welcome then, you insubstantial air that I embrace; the wretch you have blown to the worst owes nothing to your blasts.
[Enter GLOUCESTER, led by an Old Man.]
But who comes here? My father, poorly led? World, world, oh world! But for the fact that your strange mutations make us hate you, life would not yield to age.
OLD MAN. Oh my good lord, I have been your tenant, and your father's tenant, these eighty years.
GLOUCESTER. Away, go away; good friend, be gone. Your comforts can do me no good at all; you they may hurt.
OLD MAN. You cannot see your way.

GLOUCESTER. I have no way, and therefore want no eyes; I stumbled when I saw. Full often it is seen that our means make us secure, and our mere defects prove our advantages. Oh dear son Edgar, the food of your abused father's wrath! Might I but live to see you in my touch, I'd say I had eyes again!
OLD MAN. What now! Who's there?
EDGAR.
[Aside.] Oh gods! Who can say 'I am at the
worst'? I am worse than I ever was.
OLD MAN. It's poor mad Tom.
EDGAR.
[Aside.] And worse I may be yet. The worst is not
so long as we can say 'This is the worst.'
OLD MAN. Fellow, where are you going?
GLOUCESTER. Is it a beggar-man?
OLD MAN. Madman, and beggar too.

GLOUCESTER. He has some reason, else he could not beg. In last night's storm I saw such a fellow, which made me think a man no more than a worm. My son came then into my mind, and yet my mind was then scarcely friendly with him. I have heard more since. As flies to wanton boys are we to the gods — they kill us for their sport.
EDGAR.
[Aside.] How can this be?
It's a bad trade that must play fool to sorrow, angering itself and others. Bless you, master!
GLOUCESTER. Is that the naked fellow?
OLD MAN. Yes, my lord.

GLOUCESTER. Then please go away. If for my sake you will overtake us, a mile or two from here, on the way toward Dover, do it for our old love, and bring some covering for this naked soul, whom I'll ask to lead me.
OLD MAN. Alas, sir, he is mad.
GLOUCESTER. It is the time's plague when madmen lead the blind. Do as I bid you, or rather do as you please; above all, be gone.
OLD MAN. I'll bring him the best apparel I have, come what may.
[Exit.]
GLOUCESTER. Sirrah, naked fellow.
EDGAR. Poor Tom's a-cold.
[Aside.] I cannot keep this up much longer.
GLOUCESTER. Come here, fellow.
EDGAR.
[Aside.] And yet I must. Bless your sweet eyes, they bleed.
GLOUCESTER. Do you know the way to Dover?

EDGAR. Both stile and gate, horse-road and footpath. Poor Tom has been scared out of his good wits. Bless you, good man's son, from the foul fiend! Five fiends have been in poor Tom at once: of lust, as Obidicut; Hobbididence, prince of darkness; Mahu, of stealing; Modo, of murder; Flibbertigibbet, of mopping and mowing, who since possesses chambermaids and waiting women. So, bless you, master!

GLOUCESTER. Here, take this purse, you whom the heavens' plagues have humbled to all blows. That I am wretched makes you the happier. Heavens, deal so still! Let the superfluous and lust-dieted man, who enslaves your law, who will not see because he does not feel, feel your power quickly; so that distribution should undo excess, and each man have enough. Do you know Dover?
EDGAR. Yes, master.

GLOUCESTER. There is a cliff, whose high and bending head looks fearfully into the confined deep. Bring me but to the very edge of it, and I'll repair the misery you bear with something rich about me. From that place I shall need no leading.
EDGAR. Give me your arm. Poor Tom shall lead you.
[Exeunt.]

chapters.title: Act 4, Scene 2 — Before the Duke of Albany’s Palace
paragraphs: [Enter GONERIL and EDMUND; OSWALD meeting them.]
GONERIL. Welcome, my lord. I marvel our mild husband has not met us on the way. Now, where's your master?

OSWALD. Madam, within; but never a man so changed. I told him of the army that was landed; he smiled at it. I told him you were coming; his answer was, 'The worse.' Of Gloucester's treachery and of the loyal service of his son, when I informed him, then he called me a sot, and told me I had turned the wrong side out. What most he should dislike seems pleasant to him; what he should like, offensive.
GONERIL.
[To EDMUND.] Then you shall go no further.

It is the cowish terror of his spirit that dares not undertake. He won't feel wrongs that tie him to an answer. Our wishes on the way may prove effective. Back, Edmund, to my brother; hasten his musters and conduct his forces. I must change names at home, and give the distaff into my husband's hands. This trusty servant shall pass between us. Before long you are likely to hear, if you dare venture in your own behalf, a mistress's command. [Giving a favour.] Wear this; spare speech; bend down your head. This kiss, if it dared to speak, would stretch your spirits up into the air. Conceive my meaning, and farewell.
EDMUND. Yours in the ranks of death.
[Exit EDMUND.]
GONERIL. My most dear Gloucester! Oh, the difference between man and man! To you a woman's services are due; my fool of a husband usurps my body.
OSWALD. Madam, here comes my lord.
[Exit.]
[Enter ALBANY.]
GONERIL. I used to be worth the whistle.

ALBANY. Oh Goneril! You are not worth the dust which the rude wind blows in your face! I fear your disposition. That nature which despises its origin cannot be reliably contained within itself. She who will split off and break herself from her parent sap must necessarily wither and come to deadly use.
GONERIL. No more; the text is foolish.

ALBANY. Wisdom and goodness seem vile to the vile; filth savours only itself. What have you done? Tigers, not daughters, what have you performed? A father, and a gracious aged man, whose reverence even the head-collared bear would lick — most barbarously, most degenerately, have you driven mad. Could my good brother allow you to do it? A man, a prince, by him so favoured! If the heavens do not quickly send down their visible spirits to tame these vile offences, it will come — humanity must of necessity prey on itself, like monsters of the deep.

GONERIL. Milk-livered man! Who bears a cheek for blows, a head for wrongs; who has not in your brow an eye discerning your honour from your suffering; who does not know that fools pity those villains who are punished before they have done their mischief. Where's your drum? France spreads his banners in our noiseless land; with plumed helmet your kingdom begins to be threatened, while you, a moral fool, sit still and cry 'Alas, why does he so?'
ALBANY. See yourself, devil! Proper deformity does not look so horrid in the fiend as in a woman.
GONERIL. Oh, vain fool!

ALBANY. You changed and self-covered thing, for shame! Don't disfigure your face with monstrousness! If it were proper for me to let these hands obey my blood, they are apt enough to dislocate and tear your flesh and bones. However much you are a fiend, a woman's shape protects you.
GONERIL. Marry, your manhood — mew!
[Enter a Messenger.]
ALBANY. What news?
MESSENGER. Oh, my good lord, the Duke of Cornwall's dead — slain by his servant, while going to put out the other eye of Gloucester.
ALBANY. Gloucester's eyes!

MESSENGER. A servant that he had raised, struck with remorse, opposed against the act, turning his sword on his great master; who, enraged at this, flew on him, and between them they felled him dead; but not without that harmful blow which since has dragged him after.
ALBANY. This shows you are above, you justices, that these our crimes here below can be so speedily avenged! But, oh poor Gloucester! Did he lose his other eye?
MESSENGER. Both, both, my lord. This letter, madam, craves a speedy answer; it's from your sister.
GONERIL.
[Aside.] One way I like this well;
but, being a widow, and my Gloucester with her, may all the buildings in my fancy fall upon my hateful life. Another way, the news is not so bitter. I'll read and answer.
[Exit.]
ALBANY. Where was his son when they put out his eyes?
MESSENGER. Come with my lady here.
ALBANY. He is not here.
MESSENGER. No, my good lord; I met him going back.
ALBANY. Does he know about the wickedness?
MESSENGER. Yes, my good lord. It was he who informed against him; and he left the house on purpose, so that their punishment might have the freer course.
ALBANY. Gloucester, I live to thank you for the love you showed the King, and to revenge your eyes. Come here, friend, tell me what more you know.
[Exeunt.]

chapters.title: Act 4, Scene 3 — The French camp near Dover
paragraphs: [Enter KENT and a Gentleman.]
KENT. Why has the King of France so suddenly gone back? Do you know any reason?

GENTLEMAN. Something he left imperfect in the state, which since his departure has been remembered, which carries with it so much fear and danger for the kingdom that his personal return was most needed and necessary.
KENT. Whom has he left behind as general?
GENTLEMAN. The Marshal of France, Monsieur La Far.
KENT. Did your letters move the queen to any show of grief?

GENTLEMAN. Yes, sir; she took them, read them in my presence; and now and then a big tear trickled down her delicate cheek. It seemed she was a queen over her passion; which, most rebel-like, sought to be king over her.
KENT. Oh, then it moved her.

GENTLEMAN. Not to a rage. Patience and sorrow strove which should express her most becomingly. You have seen sunshine and rain at once: her smiles and tears were like a better day. Those happy little smiles that played on her ripe lips seemed not to know what guests were in her eyes; which parted from there like pearls dropped from diamonds. In brief, sorrow would be a rarity most beloved, if all could so become it.
KENT. Did she ask any verbal question?

GENTLEMAN. Indeed, once or twice she breathed out the name of 'father' pantingly, as if it pressed her heart; cried 'Sisters, sisters! Shame of ladies! Sisters! Kent! Father! Sisters! What, in the storm? In the night? Let pity not be believed!' There she shook the holy water from her heavenly eyes, and crying out mastered her; then away she started to deal with grief alone.
KENT. It is the stars, the stars above us, that govern our conditions; otherwise one self-same mate and partner couldn't beget such different children. You haven't spoken with her since?
GENTLEMAN. No.
KENT. Was this before the King returned?
GENTLEMAN. No, since.
KENT. Well, sir, the poor distressed Lear is in the town; who sometimes, in his better moments, remembers what we are come about, and by no means will yield to see his daughter.
GENTLEMAN. Why, good sir?

KENT. A sovereign shame so elbows him. His own unkindness, that stripped her from his benediction, turned her to foreign chances, gave her dear rights to his dog-hearted daughters — these things sting his mind so venomously that burning shame keeps him from Cordelia.
GENTLEMAN. Alas, poor gentleman!
KENT. Of Albany's and Cornwall's forces you have heard nothing?
GENTLEMAN. It is so; they are on the march.

KENT. Well, sir, I'll bring you to our master Lear and leave you to attend him. Some important cause will keep me concealed for a while. When I am known properly, you shall not regret making my acquaintance. I beg you, come along with me.
[Exeunt.]

chapters.title: Act 4, Scene 4 — The French camp. A Tent
paragraphs: [Enter, with drum and colours, CORDELIA, a Physician, and Soldiers.]

CORDELIA. Alas, it's he. Why, he was met just now as mad as the troubled sea; singing aloud; crowned with rank fumiter and furrow weeds, with burdocks, hemlock, nettles, cuckoo-flowers, darnel, and all the idle weeds that grow in our sustaining corn. Send forth a hundred soldiers; search every acre in the high-grown field, and bring him to our sight.
[Exit an Officer.]
What can a man's wisdom do in restoring his lost senses? He who helps him, take all my outward worth.
PHYSICIAN. There is a means, madam. Our foster nurse of nature is repose, which he lacks; to provoke that in him there are many simple remedies effective, whose power will close the eye of anguish.

CORDELIA. All blessed secrets, all you unpublished virtues of the earth, spring forth with my tears! Be helpful and remedial in this good man's distress! Seek, seek for him; lest his ungoverned rage dissolve the life that wants the means to lead it.
[Enter a Messenger.]
MESSENGER. News, madam: the British forces are marching this way.

CORDELIA. It is known already. Our preparation stands in expectation of them. Oh dear father, it is your business that I go about; therefore great France has pitied my mourning and urgent tears. No swollen ambition incites our armies, but love, dear love, and our aged father's right. Soon may I hear and see him!
[Exeunt.]

chapters.title: Act 4, Scene 5 — A Room in Gloucester’s Castle
paragraphs: [Enter REGAN and OSWALD.]
REGAN. But are my brother's forces set out?
OSWALD. Yes, madam.
REGAN. Himself in person there?
OSWALD. Madam, with much fuss. Your sister is the better soldier.
REGAN. Lord Edmund didn't speak with your lord at home?
OSWALD. No, madam.
REGAN. What might my sister's letter to him be about?
OSWALD. I don't know, lady.

REGAN. Truly, he has hurried off on serious business. It was great folly, with Gloucester's eyes put out, to let him live. Wherever he arrives, he moves all hearts against us. Edmund, I think, has gone in pity of his misery, to dispatch his benighted life; and also to spy out the strength of the enemy.
OSWALD. I must follow after him, madam, with my letter.
REGAN. Our troops set out tomorrow; stay with us. The roads are dangerous.
OSWALD. I may not, madam. My lady charged me with this duty in this business.
REGAN. Why should she write to Edmund? Could you not convey her purposes by word? Perhaps — there are some things, I don't know what. I'll be very fond of you. Let me unseal the letter.
OSWALD. Madam, I had rather not —

REGAN. I know your lady does not love her husband. I am sure of that. And at her late being here, she gave strange amorous glances and most speaking looks to noble Edmund. I know you are in her confidence.
OSWALD. I, madam?

REGAN. I speak with understanding; you are, I know it. Therefore I advise you to take this note: my lord is dead; Edmund and I have spoken, and he is more suitable for my hand than for your lady's. You may gather the rest. If you do find him, please give him this; and when your mistress hears this much from you, I pray you to ask her to call her wisdom back to her. So, farewell. If you do chance to hear of that blind traitor, preferment falls on him who cuts him off.
OSWALD. Would I could meet him, madam! I should show what party I do follow.
REGAN. Farewell.
[Exeunt.]

chapters.title: Act 4, Scene 6 — The country near Dover
paragraphs: [Enter GLOUCESTER, and EDGAR dressed like a peasant.]
GLOUCESTER. When shall I come to the top of that same hill?
EDGAR. You are climbing up it now. Look how we labour.
GLOUCESTER. It seems to me the ground is level.
EDGAR. Horribly steep. Hark, do you hear the sea?
GLOUCESTER. No, truly.
EDGAR. Why then, your other senses grow imperfect because of your eyes' anguish.
GLOUCESTER. So it may be indeed. It seems to me your voice is altered, and you speak in better phrase and substance than you did.
EDGAR. You are much deceived. In nothing am I changed but in my garments.
GLOUCESTER. It seems to me you're better spoken.

EDGAR. Come on, sir; here's the place. Stand still. How fearful and dizzy it is to cast one's eyes so low! The crows and choughs that wing the midway air seem scarcely so big as beetles. Halfway down hangs one that gathers samphire — dreadful trade! It seems to me he seems no bigger than his head. The fishermen that walk upon the beach appear like mice; and yonder tall anchoring ship is diminished to her cock-boat; her cock-boat to a buoy almost too small for sight. The murmuring surge that chafes on the countless idle pebbles cannot be heard so high. I'll look no more, lest my brain turn, and my deficient sight topple me down headlong.
GLOUCESTER. Set me where you stand.
EDGAR. Give me your hand. You are now within a foot of the extreme edge. For all beneath the moon I would not leap upright.

GLOUCESTER. Let go my hand. Here, friend, is another purse; in it a jewel well worth a poor man's taking. Fairies and gods prosper it with you! Go further off; bid me farewell, and let me hear you going.
EDGAR. Now farewell, good sir.
[Seems to go.]
GLOUCESTER. With all my heart.
EDGAR.
[Aside.] Why I trifle thus with his despair
is done to cure it.

GLOUCESTER. Oh you mighty gods! This world I renounce, and in your sights patiently shake off my great affliction. If I could bear it longer, and not fall to quarrelling with your great unopposable wills, my burnt-out and loathed remnant of nature should burn itself out. If Edgar lives, oh, bless him! Now, fellow, farewell.
EDGAR. Gone, sir, farewell.
[GLOUCESTER leaps, and falls forward.]

And yet I don't know how imagination may rob the treasury of life when life itself yields to the theft. Had he been where he thought, by this time thought would have been past. Alive or dead? Ho, you, sir! Friend! Do you hear me, sir? Speak! Thus he might pass indeed; yet he revives. What are you, sir?
GLOUCESTER. Away, and let me die.

EDGAR. Had you been anything but gossamer, feathers, air, falling so many fathoms down, you'd have shattered like an egg; but you breathe, have heavy substance, do not bleed, speak, are sound. Ten masts end to end do not make the altitude from which you have perpendicularly fallen. Your life is a miracle. Speak again.
GLOUCESTER. But have I fallen, or not?
EDGAR. From the dread summit of this chalky border. Look up on high: the shrill-throated lark so far cannot be seen or heard. Just look up.

GLOUCESTER. Alas, I have no eyes. Is wretchedness deprived of that benefit, to end itself by death? It was at least some comfort when misery could beguile the tyrant's rage and frustrate his proud will.
EDGAR. Give me your arm. Up, so. How is it? Can you feel your legs? You stand.
GLOUCESTER. Too well, too well.
EDGAR. This is above all strangeness. Upon the crown of the cliff, what thing was that which parted from you?
GLOUCESTER. A poor unfortunate beggar.

EDGAR. As I stood here below, it seemed to me his eyes were two full moons; he had a thousand noses, horns whelked and waved like the enraged sea. It was some fiend. Therefore, you happy father, think that the clearest gods, who make their honours out of men's impossibilities, have preserved you.

GLOUCESTER. I do remember now. From now on I'll bear affliction till it cries out itself 'Enough, enough,' and dies. That thing you speak of, I took it for a man; often it would say, 'The fiend, the fiend.' He led me to that place.
EDGAR. Bear free and patient thoughts. But who comes here?
[Enter LEAR, fantastically dressed up with flowers.]
The sane sense will never accommodate its master like this.
LEAR. No, they cannot arrest me for coining. I am the King himself.
EDGAR. Oh, you side-piercing sight!

LEAR. Nature is above art in that respect. There's your press-money. That fellow handles his bow like a scarecrow: draw me a clothier's yard. Look, look, a mouse! Peace, peace; this piece of toasted cheese will do it. There's my gauntlet; I'll prove it against a giant. Bring up the brown bills. Oh, well flown, bird! In the clout, in the clout. Hewgh! Give the password.
EDGAR. Sweet marjoram.
LEAR. Pass.
GLOUCESTER. I know that voice.

LEAR. Ha! Goneril with a white beard! They flattered me like a dog, and told me I had white hairs in my beard before the black ones were there. To say 'aye' and 'no' to everything I said 'aye' and 'no' to was no good theology. When the rain came to wet me once, and the wind made me chatter; when the thunder would not be silent at my bidding; there I found them, there I smelt them out. Go to, they are not men of their words. They told me I was everything; it's a lie, I am not ague-proof.
GLOUCESTER. The trick of that voice I remember well. Is it not the King?

LEAR. Yes, every inch a king. When I do stare, see how the subject quakes. I pardon that man's life. What was your cause? Adultery? You shall not die. Die for adultery! No: the wren goes to it, and the small gilded fly lechers in my sight. Let copulation thrive; for Gloucester's bastard son was kinder to his father than my daughters got between the lawful sheets. To it, lust, pell-mell! For I lack soldiers. Behold yonder simpering dame, whose face between her forks foretells snow; who minces virtue, and shakes her head to hear pleasure's name. The polecat and the fed horse don't go at it with a more riotous appetite. Down from the waist they are centaurs, though women all above. But only to the girdle do the gods inherit them; beneath is all the fiend's: there's hell, there's darkness, there is the sulphurous pit; burning, scalding, stench, consumption. Fie, fie, fie! Pah, pah! Give me an ounce of civet, good apothecary, to sweeten my imagination. There's money for you.
GLOUCESTER. Oh, let me kiss that hand!
LEAR. Let me wipe it first; it smells of mortality.
GLOUCESTER. Oh ruined piece of nature, this great world shall so wear out to nothing. Do you know me?
LEAR. I remember your eyes well enough. Do you squint at me? No, do your worst, blind Cupid; I'll not love. Read this challenge; mark just the writing of it.
GLOUCESTER. Were all the letters suns, I could not see one.
EDGAR. I would not take this from report. It is, and my heart breaks at it.
LEAR. Read.
GLOUCESTER. What, with the sockets of eyes?
LEAR. Oh ho, are you there with me? No eyes in your head, nor any money in your purse? Your eyes are in a heavy case, your purse in a light one; yet you see how this world goes.
GLOUCESTER. I see it by feeling.

LEAR. What, are you mad? A man may see how the world goes with no eyes. Look with your ears. See how that justice rails upon that simple thief. Listen in your ear: change places; and, presto-change-o, which is the justice, which is the thief? You have seen a farmer's dog bark at a beggar?
GLOUCESTER. Yes, sir.

LEAR. And the creature run from the cur? There you might behold the great image of authority: a dog is obeyed in office. You rascal beadle, hold your bloody hand! Why do you lash that whore? Strip your own back; you hotly lust to use her in that way for which you whip her. The usurer hangs the cheat. Through tattered clothes great vices appear; robes and furred gowns hide all. Plate sin with gold, and the strong lance of justice breaks harmlessly; arm it in rags, a pygmy's straw pierces it. None offends, none, I say none; I'll vouch for them. Take that from me, my friend, who have the power to seal the accuser's lips. Get yourself glass eyes, and like a scurvy politician, pretend to see the things you do not. Now, now, now, now: pull off my boots: harder, harder, so.
EDGAR. Oh, matter and impertinence mixed! Reason in madness!

LEAR. If you will weep my fortunes, take my eyes. I know you well enough; your name is Gloucester. You must be patient; we came crying here. You know the first time that we smell the air, we wail and cry. I will preach to you: mark.
GLOUCESTER. Alas, alas the day!

LEAR. When we are born, we cry that we have come to this great stage of fools. This is a good block. It would be a delicate stratagem to shoe a troop of horses with felt. I'll put it to the test, and when I have stolen up on these sons-in-law, then kill, kill, kill, kill, kill, kill!
[Enter a Gentleman with Attendants.]
GENTLEMAN. Oh, here he is; lay hands on him. Sir, your most dear daughter —
LEAR. No rescue? What, a prisoner? I am the very natural fool of fortune. Use me well; you shall have ransom. Let me have surgeons; I am cut to the brains.
GENTLEMAN. You shall have anything.
LEAR. No seconds? All myself? Why, this would make a man a man of salt, to use his eyes for garden water-pots — yes, and for laying autumn's dust.
GENTLEMAN. Good sir.
LEAR. I will die bravely, like a smug bridegroom. What! I will be jovial. Come, come, I am a king, my masters, you know that.
GENTLEMAN. You are a royal one, and we obey you.
LEAR. Then there's life in it. Come, and you get it, you shall get it by running. Sa, sa, sa, sa!
[Exit running. Attendants follow.]
GENTLEMAN. A sight most pitiful in the meanest wretch, past speaking of in a king! You have one daughter who redeems nature from the general curse which the two have brought it to.
EDGAR. Hail, gentle sir.
GENTLEMAN. Sir, may you speed. What is your wish?
EDGAR. Do you hear anything, sir, of a battle approaching?
GENTLEMAN. Most certain and well-known. Everyone hears that, who can distinguish sound.
EDGAR. But, by your favour, how near is the other army?
GENTLEMAN. Near, and on speedy march. The main sighting is expected any hour.
EDGAR. I thank you, sir; that's all.
GENTLEMAN. Though the queen on special cause is here, her army has moved on.
EDGAR. I thank you, sir.
[Exit Gentleman.]
GLOUCESTER. You ever-gentle gods, take my breath from me; let not my worse spirit tempt me again to die before you please.
EDGAR. Well prayed, father.
GLOUCESTER. Now, good sir, what are you?
EDGAR. A most poor man, made tame to fortune's blows; who, by the art of known and felt sorrows, am full of ready pity. Give me your hand, I'll lead you to some shelter.
GLOUCESTER. Hearty thanks. The bounty and the blessing of heaven on top of it, and on top of that.
[Enter OSWALD.]

OSWALD. A proclaimed prize! Most happy! That eyeless head of yours was first formed of flesh to raise my fortunes. You old unhappy traitor, briefly recollect yourself. The sword is out that must destroy you.
GLOUCESTER. Now let your friendly hand put strength enough to it.
[EDGAR steps between them.]
OSWALD. Why, bold peasant, do you dare to support a published traitor? Hence, lest the infection of his fortune take like hold on you. Let go of his arm.
EDGAR. I'll not let go, sir, without further occasion.
OSWALD. Let go, slave, or you die!

EDGAR. Good gentleman, go your way, and let poor folk pass. If I could have been bullied out of my life, it would not have been so long as it is by a fortnight. Nay, don't come near the old man; keep off, I warn ye, or I'll try whether your head or my cudgel be the harder. I'll be plain with you.
OSWALD. Out, dunghill!
EDGAR. I'll pick your teeth, sir. Come! Never mind your thrusts.
[They fight, and EDGAR knocks him down.]

OSWALD. Slave, you have slain me. Villain, take my purse. If ever you would thrive, bury my body; and give the letters that you find about me to Edmund, Earl of Gloucester. Seek him out on the British side. Oh, untimely death!
[Dies.]
EDGAR. I know you well. A serviceable villain, as dutiful to the vices of your mistress as badness could desire.
GLOUCESTER. What, is he dead?

EDGAR. Sit down, father; rest yourself. Let me look at these pockets; the letters he speaks of may be my friends. He's dead; I am only sorry he had no other executioner. Let us see. Leave, gentle wax; and, manners, don't blame us. To know our enemies' minds, we'd rip their hearts; opening their papers is more lawful.
[Reads.] 'Let our mutual vows be remembered. You have many

opportunities to cut him off; if your will is not wanting, time and place will be fruitfully offered. There is nothing done if he returns the conqueror: then I am the prisoner, and his bed my gaol; from the loathed warmth of which deliver me, and supply the place for your labour. Your (wife, so I would say) affectionate servant, Goneril.' Oh undefined space of woman's will! A plot upon her virtuous husband's life, and the exchange my brother! Here in the sands I'll bury you, the unholy messenger of murderous lechers; and in the ripe time, with this graceless paper strike the sight of the death-plotted Duke. For him, it is well that I can tell of your death and your business.
[Exit EDGAR, dragging out the body.]

GLOUCESTER. The King is mad: how stubborn is my vile sense, that I stand upright, and have keen feeling of my huge sorrows! Better I were deranged: then my thoughts would be severed from my griefs, and woes by wrong imaginations lose the knowledge of themselves.
[A drum far off.]
EDGAR. Give me your hand. Far off it seems to me I hear the beaten drum. Come, father, I'll place you with a friend.
[Exeunt.]

chapters.title: Act 4, Scene 7 — A Tent in the French Camp
paragraphs: [LEAR on a bed, asleep, soft music playing; Physician, Gentleman, and others attending.]
[Enter CORDELIA and KENT.]
CORDELIA. Oh you good Kent, how shall I live and work to match your goodness? My life will be too short, and every measure fail me.
KENT. To be acknowledged, madam, is overpaid. All my reports go with the modest truth; nor more, nor cut short, but just so.
CORDELIA. Be better dressed. These weeds are reminders of those worse hours; please put them off.
KENT. Pardon, dear madam; yet to be known shortens my settled intent. My favour I make this: that you not know me till time and I think it fitting.
CORDELIA. Then let it be so, my good lord. [To the Physician.] How is the King?
PHYSICIAN. Madam, still sleeps.
CORDELIA. Oh you kind gods, cure this great breach in his abused nature! The untuned and jarring senses, oh, restore again in this child-changed father.
PHYSICIAN. If it please your majesty that we may wake the King: he has slept long.
CORDELIA. Be guided by your knowledge, and proceed according to your own will. Is he dressed?
PHYSICIAN. Yes, madam. In the heaviness of sleep we put fresh garments on him. Be by, good madam, when we do wake him; I do not doubt his calmness.
CORDELIA. Very well.
PHYSICIAN. Please, draw near. Louder the music there!
CORDELIA. Oh my dear father! May restoration hang its medicine on my lips, and let this kiss repair those violent harms that my two sisters have inflicted on your reverence!
KENT. Kind and dear princess!

CORDELIA. Had you not been their father, these white flakes would have challenged pity from them. Was this a face to be set against the warring winds? To stand against the deep dread-bolted thunder? In the most terrible and nimble stroke of quick crossed lightning? To watch — poor sentry! — with this thin helm? My enemy's dog, though he had bitten me, should have stood that night against my fire; and were you forced, poor father, to take shelter with swine and outcast rogues in short and musty straw? Alas, alas! It is a wonder that your life and wits at once didn't end everything. He wakes; speak to him.
PHYSICIAN. Madam, you speak to him; it is most fitting.
CORDELIA. How does my royal lord? How fares your majesty?
LEAR. You do me wrong to take me out of the grave. You are a soul in bliss; but I am bound upon a wheel of fire, so that my own tears scald like molten lead.
CORDELIA. Sir, do you know me?
LEAR. You are a spirit, I know. When did you die?
CORDELIA. Still, still, far astray!
PHYSICIAN. He's scarcely awake; let him alone a while.

LEAR. Where have I been? Where am I? Fair daylight? I am greatly abused. I should even die with pity to see another like this. I don't know what to say. I won't swear these are my hands. Let's see; I feel this pin prick. Would I were certain of my condition!
CORDELIA. Oh, look upon me, sir, and hold your hands in blessing over me. No, sir, you must not kneel.

LEAR. Please, do not mock me. I am a very foolish, fond old man, fourscore and upward, not an hour more nor less; and, to deal plainly, I fear I am not in my perfect mind. It seems to me I should know you, and know this man; yet I am doubtful, for I am mainly ignorant what place this is, and all the skill I have does not recognise these garments; nor do I know where I lodged last night. Do not laugh at me, for, as I am a man, I think this lady to be my child Cordelia.
CORDELIA. And so I am. I am.

LEAR. Are your tears wet? Yes, indeed. I pray you, do not weep. If you have poison for me, I will drink it. I know you do not love me, for your sisters have, as I remember, done me wrong. You have some cause, they have not.
CORDELIA. No cause, no cause.
LEAR. Am I in France?
KENT. In your own kingdom, sir.
LEAR. Do not deceive me.

PHYSICIAN. Be comforted, good madam; the great rage, you see, is killed in him. And yet it is dangerous to make him try to recall the time he has lost. Ask him to go in; trouble him no more till he is further settled.
CORDELIA. Will it please your highness to walk?
LEAR. You must bear with me. I pray you now, forget and forgive. I am old and foolish.
[Exeunt LEAR, CORDELIA, Physician, and Attendants.]
GENTLEMAN. Is it true, sir, that the Duke of Cornwall was so slain?
KENT. Most certain, sir.
GENTLEMAN. Who leads his people?
KENT. As it is said, the bastard son of Gloucester.
GENTLEMAN. They say Edgar, his banished son, is with the Earl of Kent in Germany.
KENT. Report is changeable. It is time to look about; the forces of the kingdom approach quickly.
GENTLEMAN. The decision is likely to be bloody. Farewell, sir.
[Exit.]
KENT. My point and period will be wrought thoroughly, either well or ill, as this day's battle is fought.
[Exit.]

chapters.title: Act 5, Scene 1 — The Camp of the British Forces near Dover
paragraphs: [Enter, with drum and colours, EDMUND, REGAN, Officers, Soldiers, and others.]

EDMUND. Find out from the Duke if his last purpose holds, or whether since then he has been advised by anything to change the course; he's full of alteration and self-reproach. Bring his settled decision.
[To an Officer, who goes out.]
REGAN. Our sister's man has certainly come to grief.
EDMUND. It is to be feared, madam.
REGAN. Now, sweet lord, you know the goodness I intend toward you. Tell me but truly, but then speak the truth: do you not love my sister?
EDMUND. In honoured love.
REGAN. But have you never found my brother's way to the forbidden place?
EDMUND. That thought wrongs you.
REGAN. I have a doubt that you have been joined and intimate with her, as far as we say is hers.
EDMUND. No, by my honour, madam.
REGAN. I never shall endure her. Dear my lord, do not be familiar with her.
EDMUND. Fear not. She and the Duke her husband!
[Enter, with drum and colours, ALBANY, GONERIL, and Soldiers.]
GONERIL.
[Aside.] I had rather lose the battle than that sister
should loosen him from me.

ALBANY. Our very loving sister, well met. Sir, this I heard: the King has come to his daughter, with others whom the rigour of our state forced to cry out. Where I could not be honest, I never yet was valiant. For this business, it touches us in that France invades our land, not because it emboldens the King, with others whom, I fear, most just and heavy causes have made oppose us.
EDMUND. Sir, you speak nobly.
REGAN. Why is this being argued?
GONERIL. Combine together against the enemy; for these domestic and particular quarrels are not the question here.
ALBANY. Let us then determine with the experienced of war on our proceeding.
EDMUND. I shall attend you presently at your tent.
REGAN. Sister, will you go with us?
GONERIL. No.
REGAN. It is most fitting; please, go with us.
GONERIL.
[Aside.] Oh ho, I know the riddle. I will go.
[Exeunt EDMUND, REGAN, GONERIL, Officers, Soldiers, and Attendants.]
[As they are going out, enter EDGAR disguised.]
EDGAR. If ever your grace had speech with a man so poor, hear me one word.
ALBANY. I'll overtake you. Speak.

EDGAR. Before you fight the battle, open this letter. If you have victory, let the trumpet sound for the man who brought it. Wretched though I seem, I can produce a champion who will prove what is asserted there. If you miscarry, your business of the world has its end, and plotting ceases. Fortune love you!
ALBANY. Stay till I have read the letter.
EDGAR. I was forbidden it. When the time shall serve, just let the herald cry, and I'll appear again.
ALBANY. Why, farewell. I will look over your paper.
[Exit EDGAR.]
[Enter EDMUND.]
EDMUND. The enemy is in view; draw up your forces. Here is the estimate of their true strength and forces by diligent discovery; but your haste is now urged on you.
ALBANY. We will meet the time.
[Exit.]

EDMUND. To both these sisters have I sworn my love; each jealous of the other, as the stung are of the adder. Which of them shall I take? Both? One? Or neither? Neither can be enjoyed if both remain alive. To take the widow exasperates and maddens her sister Goneril; and I shall hardly carry out my side, her husband being alive. Now then, we'll use his countenance for the battle; which being done, let her who would be rid of him devise his speedy taking off. As for the mercy which he intends to Lear and to Cordelia, the battle done, and they within our power, they shall never see his pardon. For my state stands upon me to defend, not to debate.
[Exit.]

chapters.title: Act 5, Scene 2 — A field between the two Camps
paragraphs: [Alarum within. Enter, with drum and colours, LEAR, CORDELIA, and their Forces, and exeunt.]
[Enter EDGAR and GLOUCESTER.]
EDGAR. Here, father, take the shadow of this tree for your good host; pray that the right may thrive. If ever I return to you again, I'll bring you comfort.
GLOUCESTER. Grace go with you, sir!
[Exit EDGAR.]
[Alarum and retreat within. Enter EDGAR.]
EDGAR. Away, old man, give me your hand, away! King Lear has lost, he and his daughter taken. Give me your hand; come on!
GLOUCESTER. No further, sir; a man may rot even here.
EDGAR. What, in ill thoughts again? Men must endure their going hence, even as their coming here; ripeness is all. Come on.
GLOUCESTER. And that's true too.
[Exeunt.]

chapters.title: Act 5, Scene 3 — The British Camp near Dover
paragraphs: [Enter in conquest, with drum and colours, EDMUND; LEAR and CORDELIA as prisoners; Officers, Soldiers, etc.]
EDMUND. Some officers, take them away. Keep good guard until their greater pleasures be first known, those who are to judge them.

CORDELIA. We are not the first who, with the best meaning, have incurred the worst. For you, oppressed King, I am cast down; otherwise I could out-frown false fortune's frown. Shall we not see these daughters and these sisters?

LEAR. No, no, no, no. Come, let's away to prison. We two alone will sing like birds in the cage. When you do ask me blessing I'll kneel down and ask of you forgiveness. So we'll live, and pray, and sing, and tell old tales, and laugh at gilded butterflies, and hear poor rogues talk of court news; and we'll talk with them too — who loses and who wins; who's in, who's out; and take upon us the mystery of things, as if we were God's spies. And we'll wear out, in a walled prison, packs and sects of great ones that ebb and flow by the moon.
EDMUND. Take them away.

LEAR. Upon such sacrifices, my Cordelia, the gods themselves throw incense. Have I caught you? He who parts us shall bring a torch from heaven, and burn us out of here like foxes. Wipe your eyes. The plagues shall devour them, flesh and skin, before they shall make us weep! We'll see them starve first. Come.
[Exeunt LEAR and CORDELIA, guarded.]

EDMUND. Come here, captain, listen. Take this note [giving a paper]; go follow them to prison. One step I have advanced you; if you do as this instructs you, you will make your way to noble fortunes. Know this: that men are as the times are. To be tender-minded does not become a sword. Your great employment will not bear question; either say you'll do it, or thrive by other means.
CAPTAIN. I'll do it, my lord.
EDMUND. To it; and call yourself fortunate when you have done. Mark, I say, instantly; and carry it out as I have set it down.
CAPTAIN. I cannot pull a cart, nor eat dried oats; if it be man's work, I'll do it.
[Exit.]
[Flourish. Enter ALBANY, GONERIL, REGAN, Officers, and Attendants.]

ALBANY. Sir, you have shown today your valiant strain, and fortune led you well. You have the captives who were the opponents of this day's strife; I do demand them of you, to use them as we shall find their merits and our safety may equally determine.

EDMUND. Sir, I thought it fit to send the old and miserable King to some confinement and appointed guard; whose age has charms in it, and whose title more, to draw the common heart to his side, and turn our conscripted lances into our own eyes that command them. With him I sent the queen; my reason all the same; and they are ready tomorrow, or at a later time, to appear where you shall hold your session. At this time we sweat and bleed: the friend has lost his friend, and the best quarrels in the heat are cursed by those who feel their sharpness. The question of Cordelia and her father requires a fitter place.
ALBANY. Sir, by your patience, I hold you but as a subject of this war, not as a brother.

REGAN. That depends on how we choose to grace him. It seems to me our pleasure might have been asked before you spoke so far. He led our forces; bore the commission of my place and person; the immediacy of which may well stand up and call itself your brother.
GONERIL. Not so hot. In his own grace he exalts himself, more than in your addition.
REGAN. In my rights, vested by me, he matches the best.
ALBANY. That would be the most, if he should become your husband.
REGAN. Jesters do often prove prophets.
GONERIL. Hello, hello! That eye that told you so was looking askew.

REGAN. Lady, I am not well; otherwise I should answer from a fully overflowing stomach. General, take my soldiers, prisoners, patrimony; dispose of them, of me; the walls are yours. Let the world witness that I create you here my lord and master.
GONERIL. Do you mean to enjoy him?
ALBANY. The forbidding does not lie in your good will.
EDMUND. Nor in yours, lord.
ALBANY. Half-blooded fellow, yes.
REGAN.
[To EDMUND.] Let the drum strike, and prove my title yours.

ALBANY. Stay yet; hear reason. Edmund, I arrest you on capital treason; and, in your arrest, this gilded serpent. [Pointing to GONERIL.] For your claim, fair sister, I bar it in the interest of my wife. It is she who is sub-contracted to this lord, and I her husband contradict your banns. If you will marry, make your love-suits to me; my lady is bespoken.
GONERIL. An interlude!

ALBANY. You are armed, Gloucester. Let the trumpet sound. If no one appears to prove upon your person your heinous, manifest, and many treasons, there is my pledge. [Throwing down a glove.] I'll prove it on your heart, before I taste bread, that you are in nothing less than I have here proclaimed you.
REGAN. Sick, oh, sick!
GONERIL.
[Aside.] If not, I'll never trust medicine.

EDMUND. There's my exchange. [Throwing down a glove.] Whatever in the world he is who names me traitor, like a villain he lies. Call by your trumpet: he who dares approach, on him, on you, who not? I will maintain my truth and honour firmly.
ALBANY. A herald, ho!
[Enter a Herald.]
Trust to your single virtue; for your soldiers, all levied in my name, have in my name been discharged.
REGAN. My sickness grows upon me.
ALBANY. She is not well. Convey her to my tent.
[Exit REGAN, led.]
Come here, herald. Let the trumpet sound, and read out this.
OFFICER. Sound, trumpet!
[A trumpet sounds.]
HERALD.
[Reads.] 'If any man of quality or rank within the lists of
the army will maintain against Edmund, supposed Earl of Gloucester, that he is a manifold traitor, let him appear by the third sound of the trumpet. He is bold in his defence.'
EDMUND. Sound!
[First trumpet.]
HERALD. Again!
[Second trumpet.]
HERALD. Again!
[Third trumpet. Trumpet answers within. Enter EDGAR, armed, preceded by a trumpet.]
ALBANY. Ask him his purposes — why he appears upon this call of the trumpet.
HERALD. What are you? Your name, your rank? And why you answer this present summons?
EDGAR. Know that my name is lost — by treason's tooth bare-gnawed and canker-bit. Yet I am as noble as the adversary I come to fight.
ALBANY. Which is that adversary?
EDGAR. Who is he that speaks for Edmund, Earl of Gloucester?
EDMUND. Himself; what do you say to him?

EDGAR. Draw your sword, so that if my speech offends a noble heart, your arm may do you justice. Here is mine. Behold, it is the privilege of my honours, my oath, and my profession: I protest, despite your strength, youth, place, and eminence, despite your victorious sword and brand-new fortune, your valour and your heart, you are a traitor; false to your gods, your brother, and your father; conspiring against this high illustrious prince; and, from the extremest top of your head to the descent and dust beneath your foot, a most toad-spotted traitor. Say you 'no,' and this sword, this arm, and my best spirits are bent to prove upon your heart, where I am speaking, that you lie.

EDMUND. In wisdom I should ask your name; but since your outside looks so fair and warlike, and your tongue breathes some token of breeding, what I might safely and properly delay by the rule of knighthood, I disdain and spurn. Back I toss those treasons to your head; with the hell-hated lie I overwhelm your heart; which, since they yet glance off and scarcely bruise, this sword of mine shall give them instant entrance, where they shall rest for ever. Trumpets, speak!
[Alarums. They fight. EDMUND falls.]
ALBANY. Save him, save him!
GONERIL. This is mere trickery, Gloucester. By the law of arms you were not bound to answer an unknown opponent. You are not vanquished, but tricked and beguiled.
ALBANY. Shut your mouth, dame, or with this paper shall I stop it. Hold, sir; you, worse than any name, read your own evil. No tearing, lady; I perceive you know it.
[Gives the letter to EDMUND.]
GONERIL. Say I do — the laws are mine, not yours. Who can arraign me for it?
[Exit.]
ALBANY. Most monstrous! Oh! Do you know this paper?
EDMUND. Ask me not what I know.
ALBANY.
[To an Officer, who goes out.] Go after her; she's desperate;
govern her.

EDMUND. What you have charged me with, that have I done; and more, much more — the time will bring it out. It's past, and so am I. But what are you, who has this fortune over me? If you are noble, I do forgive you.

EDGAR. Let's exchange charity. I am no less in blood than you are, Edmund; if more, the more you have wronged me. My name is Edgar, and I am your father's son. The gods are just, and of our pleasant vices make instruments to plague us. The dark and vicious place where he begot you cost him his eyes.
EDMUND. You have spoken right, it's true. The wheel has come full circle; I am here.
ALBANY. It seemed to me your very gait foretold a royal nobleness. I must embrace you. Let sorrow split my heart if ever I did hate you or your father.
EDGAR. Worthy prince, I know it.
ALBANY. Where have you hidden yourself? How have you known the miseries of your father?

EDGAR. By nursing them, my lord. Hear a brief tale; and when it is told, oh that my heart would burst! The bloody proclamation to escape, that followed me so closely — oh, our lives' sweetness! That with the pain of death we'd hourly die rather than die at once! — taught me to shift into a madman's rags; to assume an appearance that even dogs disdained; and in this guise I met my father with his bleeding sockets, their precious stones newly lost; became his guide, led him, begged for him, saved him from despair; never — oh fault! — revealed myself to him until some half an hour ago, when I was armed. Not sure, though hoping for this good success, I asked his blessing, and from first to last told him my pilgrimage. But his flawed heart — alas, too weak the conflict to support! — between two extremes of passion, joy and grief, burst smilingly.
EDMUND. This speech of yours has moved me, and shall perhaps do good; but go on; you look as if you had something more to say.
ALBANY. If there be more, more woeful, hold it in; for I am almost ready to dissolve, hearing of this.

EDGAR. This would have seemed an ending to such as love not sorrow; but another, by amplifying too much, would make much more, and top extremity. While I was big in clamour, there came a man who, having seen me in my worst condition, shunned my abhorred company; but then, finding who it was that so endured, with his strong arms he fastened on my neck and bellowed out as if he would burst heaven; threw himself on my father; told the most piteous tale of Lear and him that ear ever received, which in the recounting his grief grew powerful, and the strings of life began to crack. Twice then the trumpets sounded, and there I left him in a trance.
ALBANY. But who was this?
EDGAR. Kent, sir, the banished Kent; who in disguise followed his enemy king and did him service improper for a slave.
[Enter a Gentleman hastily, with a bloody knife.]
GENTLEMAN. Help, help! Oh, help!
EDGAR. What kind of help?
ALBANY. Speak, man.
EDGAR. What does this bloody knife mean?
GENTLEMAN. It is hot, it smokes; it came just now from the heart of — oh! She's dead!
ALBANY. Who dead? Speak, man.
GENTLEMAN. Your lady, sir, your lady; and her sister was poisoned by her; she has confessed it.
EDMUND. I was contracted to them both; all three now marry in an instant.
EDGAR. Here comes Kent.
[Enter KENT.]

ALBANY. Produce their bodies, whether alive or dead. This judgement of the heavens that makes us tremble touches us not with pity. Oh, is this he? The time will not allow the compliment which good manners urges.
KENT. I am come to bid my King and master forever good night. Is he not here?
ALBANY. Great thing of us forgotten! Speak, Edmund, where's the King? And where's Cordelia?
[The bodies of GONERIL and REGAN are brought in.]
Do you see this object, Kent?
KENT. Alas, why thus?
EDMUND. Yet Edmund was beloved. The one poisoned the other for my sake, and after slew herself.
ALBANY. Even so. Cover their faces.
EDMUND. I pant for life. Some good I mean to do, despite my own nature. Quickly send — be brief in it — to the castle; for my warrant is on the life of Lear and on Cordelia. Nay, send in time.
ALBANY. Run, run, oh, run!
EDGAR. To whom, my lord? Who has the commission? Send your token of reprieve.
EDMUND. Well thought of: take my sword, give it to the captain.
EDGAR. Hasten, for your life.
[Exit EDGAR.]
EDMUND. He has commission from your wife and me to hang Cordelia in the prison, and to lay the blame upon her own despair, that she destroyed herself.
ALBANY. The gods defend her! Bear him hence a while.
[EDMUND is borne off.]
[Enter LEAR with CORDELIA dead in his arms; EDGAR, Officer, and others following.]

LEAR. Howl, howl, howl, howl! Oh, you are men of stone. Had I your tongues and eyes, I'd use them so that heaven's vault should crack. She's gone for ever! I know when one is dead, and when one lives. She's dead as earth. Lend me a looking glass. If her breath will mist or stain the stone, why then she lives.
KENT. Is this the promised end?
EDGAR. Or image of that horror?
ALBANY. Fall, and cease!
LEAR. This feather stirs; she lives! If it be so, it is a chance which redeems all the sorrows that I have ever felt.
KENT. Oh, my good master! [Kneeling.]
LEAR. Please, away!
EDGAR. It is noble Kent, your friend.

LEAR. A plague upon you, murderers, traitors all! I might have saved her; now she's gone for ever! Cordelia, Cordelia! Stay a little. Ha! What is it you say? Her voice was ever soft, gentle, and low, an excellent thing in a woman. I killed the slave that was hanging you.
OFFICER. It is true, my lords, he did.

LEAR. Didn't I, fellow? I have seen the day, with my good biting falchion I would have made them skip. I am old now, and these same crosses spoil me. Who are you? My eyes are not the best, I'll tell you straight.
KENT. If Fortune brags of two she loved and hated, one of them we behold.
LEAR. This is a dull sight. Are you not Kent?
KENT. The same, your servant Kent. Where is your servant Caius?
LEAR. He's a good fellow, I can tell you that. He'll strike, and quickly too. He's dead and rotten.
KENT. No, my good lord; I am the very man.
LEAR. I'll see to that straight.
KENT. Who, from your first of difference and decay, have followed your sad steps.
LEAR. You are welcome here.
KENT. Nor any man else. All is cheerless, dark and deadly. Your eldest daughters have destroyed themselves, and desperately are dead.
LEAR. Yes, so I think.
ALBANY. He does not know what he says; and it is vain that we present ourselves to him.
EDGAR. Quite pointless.
[Enter an Officer.]
OFFICER. Edmund is dead, my lord.

ALBANY. That is but a trifle here. You lords and noble friends, know our intent. What comfort to this great ruin may come shall be applied. For us, we will resign, during the life of this old majesty, to him our absolute power;
[To EDGAR and KENT.] you to your rights;
with extra and such addition as your honours have more than merited. All friends shall taste the wages of their virtue, and all foes the cup of their deservings. Oh, see, see!

LEAR. And my poor fool is hanged! No, no, no life! Why should a dog, a horse, a rat have life, and you no breath at all? You'll come no more, never, never, never, never, never! Please undo this button. Thank you, sir. Do you see this? Look on her: look, her lips, look there, look there!
[He dies.]
EDGAR. He faints! My lord, my lord!
KENT. Break, heart; please break!
EDGAR. Look up, my lord.
KENT. Vex not his ghost. Oh, let him pass! He hates him that would upon the rack of this rough world stretch him out longer.
EDGAR. He is gone indeed.
KENT. The wonder is, he has endured so long. He but usurped his life.
ALBANY. Bear them from here. Our present business is general woe. [To EDGAR and KENT.] Friends of my soul, you two, rule in this realm and the wounded state sustain.
KENT. I have a journey, sir, shortly to go; my master calls me, I must not say no.
EDGAR. The weight of this sad time we must obey; speak what we feel, not what we ought to say. The oldest has borne most; we that are young shall never see so much, nor live so long.
[Exeunt with a dead march.]
